items.stem: In Qlik Sense, two tables share two common field names, producing an unwanted synthetic key. What is the cleanest fix?

options.text: Rename or remove one of the shared fields so a single key links the tables
options.rationale: Correct: reducing the shared fields to a single intended key removes the synthetic key.
Deleting the tables loses the data entirely.

options.text: Add a third copy of each field
options.rationale: Adding more shared fields worsens the synthetic key.

options.text: Join everything into one giant table always
options.rationale: Forcing a single flat table is not generally appropriate and may duplicate rows.

items.explanation: Correct: reducing the shared fields to a single intended key removes the synthetic key.

items.stem: Which expression sums Sales only for the year 2025 regardless of current selections?

options.rationale: Correct: the set-analysis modifier {<Year={2025}>} restricts the aggregation to 2025.
Sum(Sales) follows current selections, not a fixed year.
Only(Year) returns a year value, not a sales sum.
Count(Sales) counts rows rather than summing values.

items.explanation: Correct: the set-analysis modifier {<Year={2025}>} restricts the aggregation to 2025.

items.stem: Which TWO are advantages of using master items in a Qlik Sense app? (Select TWO)

options.text: Definitions are reused consistently across sheets
options.rationale: Correct: master items give consistent, reusable definitions across the app.

options.text: A measure's logic is maintained in one place
options.rationale: Correct: centralizing a measure means one edit updates every use.

options.text: They remove the need for a data model
options.rationale: A data model is still required; master items build on it.
Master items do not disable selections; association still applies.

items.explanation: Correct: master items give consistent, reusable definitions across the app.; Correct: centralizing a measure means one edit updates every use.
